answer: Under adverse-selection pricing, a submission's locked reward is not fixed: any established reviewer may open a short, staking bond that the answer will be downgraded at re-grade. A correct short claims part of the author's payout; a wrong one burns the staker's bond. Every weak assertion becomes a profit target, so authors must anchor each claim to independently checkable grounds up front. A farm rotating jetty, sonnet and canyon through one shell gets shorted in bulk and its bonds cascade; an honest writer pays almost nothing. Attacker cost: N defensible answers, not one refilled template.
